title: Microsoft Teams: latest meeting experience for anonymous join on Safari and Firefox web
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly excludes all signed-in users, although Microsoft says users signed in to an organisation without mutual trust can be anonymous participants. It also presents Unverified as the label for all anonymous users, overlooking Email Verified, and makes unsupported claims about browser-documentation scope and unchanged admission rules.

claims.where: What's changing; Security & identity; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Anonymous participants are people whose identities have not been verified.
claims.quote: In meetings and events hosted by your organization, anonymous users are users whose identities aren't verified.

claims.claim: Someone not signed in to Teams with a work or school account can be an anonymous participant.
claims.quote:
These users can include:
- Users who aren't signed in to Teams with a work or school account.

claims.claim: Teams marks anonymous participants as Unverified in a meeting.
claims.quote: When anonymous users join a meeting unverified, Unverified appears next to their name. If anonymous users join a meeting verified through a one-time passcode, Email Verified appears next to their name.
claims.fix: Replace the label sentence with: "When anonymous users join a meeting unverified, Teams displays Unverified next to their name."

claims.claim: The anonymous-join scope excludes signed-in users.
claims.quote: Anonymous - People whose identity can't be verified. They may be logged in to an organization without a mutual trust relationship or they may not have an account.
claims.fix: Replace "The roadmap wording means the change applies to these participants and not to signed-in users." with "The roadmap limits this change to anonymous join." Replace the impact rationale with "Low. People who notice are anonymous participants joining from Safari or Firefox."

claims.claim: Tenant-wide anonymous join is controlled in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting settings > Participants > Anonymous users can join a meeting.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings.
Under Participants, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity <policy name> -DisableAnonymousJoin $true prevents anonymous meeting join organisation-wide.
claims.quote:
To prevent anonymous participants from joining meetings in your organization, use this script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity <policy name> -DisableAnonymousJoin $true

claims.claim: Per-organiser anonymous join is controlled in Teams admin center at Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Under Meeting join & lobby, turn the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified toggle Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false prevents anonymous join to meetings organised by users or groups with that policy.
claims.quote:
To prevent anonymous participants from joining meetings organized by users or groups with this policy, use this script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowAnonymousUsersToJoinMeeting $false

claims.claim: Microsoft says the organisation-wide Anonymous users can join a meeting setting is going away.
claims.quote: The Anonymous users can join a meeting organization-wide setting is going away.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends leaving the organisation-wide setting On and managing anonymous join through the per-organiser policy.
claims.quote: We recommend leaving this setting On and using the Anonymous users can join a meeting unverified per-organizer meeting policy to manage anonymous meeting join instead.

claims.claim: Meeting-policy changes might take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes to meeting policies might take up to 24 hours to take effect.
